summary: A0 is a substantive, correctly-structured rubric whose core promise is machine checkability. On the four hash-bound findings carried by the prior round it is unresolved on all four: the HF-01 detector is inert (0 violations on the live corpus, and the 30 theorem-conclusion ledger rows are never passed to it); the G-FORM genericity/conclusion vocabulary does not cover any of the three frozen schemas; the WCC class tables import the future-asymptotic-predictability equivalence that F1 marks UNVERIFIED without an implication note; and the validation block is still null although the declared validator has already run on these exact bytes (failing). Two further detector/vocabulary mismatches (undefined per-class allowed-conclusion set; G-LIT/HF-03/HF-04 field names absent from the frozen L1) and a stale HF-14 evidence note were found independently. The artifact must be revised at a new hash; it is not gate-ready.

hard_failures.statement: The critical HF-01 detector has zero recall at this pin. It fires only on a record with claim.conclusion_type == theorem and no claim.artifact_refs (evaluation_rubric.yaml:174). Measured on the live corpus with the pinned rubric: 0 HF-01 violations; of 10,242 claim-like records 6,350 carry artifact_refs but 0 have conclusion_type=theorem; the 30 theorem-conclusion rows in the frozen L0 ledger are classified as `records`, not `claims`, by audit_run.py scan_corpus and are never passed to check_class_binding. The detector therefore cannot fire on any existing theorem record.
evidence_refs: research_map/research_map.json (498 claims; 423 with artifact_refs; 0 with conclusion_type=theorem)
hard_failures.falsifier: Show a rubric- or registry-bound mapping from ledger/theorems.jsonl rows to claim.artifact_refs (or a rubric revision naming the ledger's binding field and putting ledger theorem rows in the detector's scan scope) at a new A0 hash, plus one theorem record on which HF-01 evaluates to a definite true/false.

hard_failures.statement: A0's G-FORM vocabularies do not cover the artifacts A0 exists to gate. The genericity enum (evaluation_rubric.yaml:128) is {comeager, full_measure, open_dense, codim_ge_1, non_generic_excluded}; all three frozen schemas declare genericity.kind=residual_comeager, which A0 never names. A0 also requires conclusion_primary from each class' allowed set (:129) and HF-02 rejects 'conclusion_type not allowed for class' (:178-180), while the frozen_classes tables (:55-118) define no allowed set and never mention the schemas' canonical tokens weak_cosmic_censorship / scc_c2_future_inextendibility / scc_c0_future_inextendibility. A literal machine pass therefore rejects all three frozen schemas.
hard_failures.falsifier: A rubric revision that binds its genericity and conclusion vocabularies to VOCAB_ALIASES.json by sha256 (or adopts the canonical tokens, including residual_comeager, open_dense_escape, finite_codimension_complement and the three scc_*/weak_cosmic_censorship conclusion tokens) at a new hash, plus a literal checker run over the pinned schemas that accepts all three.

hard_failures.statement: The WCC class tables record future_asymptotic_predictability as conclusion_primary and completeness_of_I_plus / no_naked_singularity_from_I_plus as conclusion_implied (evaluation_rubric.yaml:63-64 and :113-114) with no implication_note and no UNVERIFIED marker, while F1 marks exactly that equivalence 'claimed equivalence, UNVERIFIED'. A0's own G-FORM criterion (:129-130) requires implied conclusions to carry an implication note, so the criterion is unsatisfiable against A0's own class table.
hard_failures.falsifier: A rubric revision at a new hash that either marks the WCC conclusion_implied entries with an explicit equivalence/UNVERIFIED status plus an implication_note, or supplies a frozen L1-verified citation of the equivalence, such that the :129-130 criterion is decidable for every frozen class.

hard_failures.statement: The validation block (evaluation_rubric.yaml:45-50) declares validator artifacts/audit/audit_run.py but leaves last_run / last_run_result / report_sha256 null, while line 46 states 'a rubric with no passing self-test is not a gate'. The declared validator has in fact already run on these exact rubric bytes and failed, so the artifact both records no self-test and has no passing one.

Read-only run of the pinned rubric through artifacts/audit/audit_lib.py check_class_binding over scan_corpus(artifacts, comms/outbox, ledger): 10,242 claim-like records, 0 HF-01 violations; audit_run.py:95-101 classifies ledger rows as `records` (they carry class_ids + statement_exact, not class_id + statement), so the 30 theorem rows are never passed to the detector. prior_findings_adjudication.why_not_out_of_scope: A0 puts the ledger under its G-LIT/G-AUDIT detectors and declares those checks machine-checkable; a critical detector that cannot reach the only theorem-bearing records is a defect of A0, not of the ledger.

prior_findings_adjudication.evidence: A0:128 enumerates {comeager, full_measure, open_dense, codim_ge_1, non_generic_excluded}. All three frozen schemas use genericity.kind=residual_comeager (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:142, af_scc_c2_vacuum.yaml:157, af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml:159), which is the canonical token in artifacts/formulation/VOCAB_ALIASES.json (comeager is listed there only as an accepted alias; the file's policy states aliases are for consistency checks only and must never appear in a new canonical artifact). A0 contains no alias table or mapping block and also uses open_dense / codim_ge_1 where the canonical tokens are open_dense_escape / finite_codimension_complement.
prior_findings_adjudication.why_not_resolved: schemas/f1_falsifier_tests.jsonl:10 (F1-AMB-10) resolves the conflict only through VOCAB_ALIASES.json, which A0 does not cite or bind; A0's own enum still omits the frozen canonical token.
prior_findings_adjudication.why_not_out_of_scope: The vocabulary is defined by A0's G-FORM criteria; the conflict is between A0:128 and the artifacts A0 gates.

additional_findings.statement: HF-14 (:243-252) detects status=accepted / supports_claim=true and its evidence_2026_09_11 note asserts that 'ledger/theorems.jsonl entries T-201..T-203 carry status=accepted and supports_claim=true'. In the frozen ledger (sha a1674f09...) those rows instead carry author_asserts_supports=true, acceptance_authority='...author self-assessment, not a reviewer verdict', review_status=not_independently_reviewed and content_status=verified; the tokens status and supports_claim occur 0 times in all 62 rows. The semantic self-certification pattern is present but the detector's literal fields have zero recall and the recorded evidence note does not describe the frozen bytes.
additional_findings.falsifier: A new A0 hash whose HF-14 detector names the ledger's actual fields (author_asserts_supports / review_status / acceptance_authority) and whose evidence note is re-anchored to the L0 hash, with a checker run that fires on the T-201..T-203 pattern.

class_leakage.detail: A0:82-83 explicitly forbids citing an SCC-C0 result as C2 evidence, and A0:85 states the correct direction (C0 implies C2, not conversely); A0:95 encodes C0 -> C2 in conclusion_implied. No C2 statement is smuggled into the C0 class and no C0/C2 merge appears. Separately, A0's class vocabularies cannot be machine-matched to the schemas (A0R3-VOCAB-DISCONNECT, A0R3-ALLOWEDSET-UNDEFINED).

conclusion_inflation.detail: See A0R3-CONCL-EQUIV-UNVERIFIED. No theorem/counterexample promotion by A0 itself was found; the header at A0:2 is explicitly draft-for-gate and all gate verdicts are pending, so HF-14 does not apply to A0's own status.

assumption_completeness.detail: Every frozen class carries dimension/asymptotics/matter_model/symmetry/cosmological_constant/formulation and a forbidden_evidence list (A0:55-68, 69-85, 86-104, 105-118). No class-level assumption required by the cited theorems is silently absent from A0's class table; HF-06 is a schema-level detector whose target fields live in the schemas, not in A0.

falsifier_decidability.detail: A0:131 requires a finite checkable falsifier in the stated topology, but the four frozen class entries carry no class-level falsifiers and no detector field; decidability lives in the schemas. This is subsumed by the vocabulary findings and not counted separately.

fields_two_readers_disagree_on.detail: The machine_checkable: true claims at A0:19 and A0:34/A0:40 depend on fields that do not exist in the frozen inputs (claim.artifact_refs, resolution_status, quantity_check, the per-class allowed conclusion set, HF-14 status/supports_claim). Two careful readers applying A0 literally to the frozen artifacts would reach opposite G-FORM/G-LIT verdicts: reject-all (vocabulary) vs pass (intended semantics).
